fixed_statement:
Let \(\Dr(F_7)\) be the poset of tropical linear subspaces of \(\Trop(F_7)\), ordered by inclusion.
Let \(\Dr_1\) be the points of \(\Trop(F_7)\), and let \(\Dr_2\) be the tropical lines contained in \(\Trop(F_7)\).
The tropical linear space \(\Trop(F_7)\) has rank \(3\).
Any inclusion-reversing involution \(\Phi\) on \(\Dr(F_7)\) restricts to a bijection \(\Dr_1\leftrightarrow \Dr_2\).
fixed_proof: Since points are the atoms of \(\Dr(F_7)\), any inclusion-reversing involution \(\Phi\) on \(\Dr(F_7)\) maps atoms to coatoms. Atoms cover only the empty set, and an inclusion-reversing involution sends covering relations at the bottom of the poset to covering relations at the top. As \(\Trop(F_7)\) has rank \(3\), the coatoms are precisely the rank \(2\) spaces. In rank \(3\), the elements covered only by the top element are the rank \(2\) tropical linear spaces. Thus \(\Phi\) restricts to a bijection \(\Dr_1\leftrightarrow \Dr_2\).
